[{"type":"page","title":"Summary","subtitle":"The numbers that matter"},{"type":"blank","content":"

Microsoft 365 is bought per person, per plan, per month. Every plan bundles a set of services, and each person is meant to hold the plan that matches what they do. Over time that drifts: people leave, roles change, and plans bought for one reason keep renewing. This report compares what Contoso (sample data) pays for with what its people actually used over the last 90 days.

These people hold plans that include no device management, no advanced sign-in protection and no device threat protection. That is a business risk rather than a saving, so the figure below is an added cost. It is the cheapest plan that gives them all three.

","title":"People with no security protection"},{"type":"richtable","columns":[{"key":"from","header":"Current plans","bold":true,"width":2.4},{"key":"to","header":"Suggested","width":2},{"align":"right","key":"seats","header":"People","width":0.7},{"align":"right","key":"unit","header":"Extra per person","width":1.2},{"align":"right","key":"delta","header":"Extra per month","width":1.3}],"rows":[{"from":"Exchange Online (Plan 1) + Microsoft 365 Apps for business","to":"Microsoft 365 Business Premium","seats":"1","unit":"$9.75","delta":"$10"},{"from":"Microsoft 365 Business Standard","to":"Microsoft 365 Business Premium","seats":"12","unit":"$9.50","delta":"$114"}],"limit":15},{"type":"page","title":"Yearly or monthly","subtitle":"Committing to the seats that will stay"},{"type":"blank","content":"

Microsoft sells the same plan two ways. A yearly commitment is cheaper but cannot be reduced until it renews. A monthly commitment costs about 20% more but can be dropped at any time. The right mix is to commit yearly to the seats that will still be there in a year and keep the rest monthly. A seat that has been with the same person for 6 months or more is treated as one that will stay.
